chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Sinani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Tamim ibn Bahlul narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

I was with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) during his march to Siffin. When he halted at Naynawa, on the bank of the Euphrates, he called out at the top of his voice: 'O Ibn Abbas, do you recognize this place?' I said to him: 'I do not recognize it, O Commander of the Faithful.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'If you knew it as I know it, you would not pass through it without weeping as I weep.' He then wept at length until his beard was drenched and tears flowed down his chest, and we wept with him. He was saying: 'Alas, alas! What is it between me and the family of Abu Sufyan, what is it between me and the family of Harb, the party of Satan and allies of disbelief! Be patient, O Abu Abdullah — for your father has endured the like of what you shall endure from them.' Then he called for water, performed wudu as for prayer, and prayed as much as Allah willed him to pray. Then he recalled words similar to his first speech, except that he dozed off for a moment at the conclusion of his prayer and speech, then

he awakened and said: 'O Ibn Abbas.' I replied: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Shall I not tell you what I saw in my sleep just now, during my brief rest?' I said: 'May your eyes sleep soundly and may you see good, O Commander of the Faithful.' He said: 'I saw as though men had descended from the sky, bearing white banners, girded with their swords — gleaming white swords — and they had drawn a circle around this land. Then I saw as though these palm trees had struck the earth with their branches, quivering in a pool of fresh blood. And as though al-Husayn — my little lamb, my fledgling, my morsel, and my very marrow — had sunk into it, crying for help but receiving none. And as though the white men had descended from the sky, calling out to him and saying: Be patient, O family of the Messenger, for you shall be slain by the hands of the worst of people, and Paradise — O Abu Abdullah — longs for you. Then they consoled me, saying: O Abu al-Hasan, rejoice, for Allah has gladdened your eyes by him

on the Day of Resurrection, the day when people will stand before the Lord of the worlds.' Then I woke up just like that. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ali, the Truthful and Verified One — Abu al-Qasim (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) — told me that I shall see it during my march against those who have transgressed against us. This is the land of tribulation and trial; al-Husayn will be buried in it, along with seventeen men from my sons and the sons of Fatima. And it is known in the heavens; the land of tribulation and trial is mentioned as the precinct of the Two Sanctuaries and the precinct of Bayt al-Maqdis are mentioned.' He then said: 'O Ibn Abbas, seek for me the dung of the gazelles around it. By Allah, I have neither lied nor been called a liar — and it is yellowed, its color is the color of saffron.' Ibn Abbas said: I searched for it and found it gathered together, so I called out to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have found it with the very description you described to me.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth.' He then rose (peace be upon him)

(peace be upon him) and hurried toward it, picked it up, smelled it, and said: 'It is it, the very same! Do you know, O Ibn Abbas, what this dung is? This is what Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him) smelled — and that was when he passed by here with the Apostles and saw the gazelles gathered here, weeping. So Jesus (peace be upon him) sat down, and the Apostles sat with him, and he wept and the Apostles wept, though they did not know why he had sat down or why he was weeping. They said: O Spirit of God and His Word, what makes you weep? He said: Do you know what land this is? They said: No. He said: This is a land in which the fledgling of the Messenger Ahmad will be killed, and the fledgling of the free, pure, and virgin one who resembles my mother, and he will be buried in it. The soil is more fragrant than musk, for it is the soil of the slain fledgling — and such is the soil of prophets and sons of prophets. These gazelles speak to me and say that they graze in this land out of longing for the soil of the blessed fledgling, and they claim to be safe in this land.' Then he struck his hand toward these droppings, smelled them, and said: 'These are the droppings of the gazelles, fragrant in this way because of the grass of this place.

O Allah, preserve them forever until his father smells them, so that they may be a consolation and comfort to him.' He said: They remained until this day of the people, and had turned yellow from the length of time. 'This is the land of tribulation and trial.' Then he called out at the top of his voice: 'O Lord of Jesus son of Mary, do not bless his killers, nor those who aided against him, nor those who abandoned him.' Then he wept with long weeping, and we wept with him, until he fell face down and lost consciousness for a long time. Then he recovered, took the dung, tied it in his garment, and ordered me to tie it up likewise. Then he said: 'O Ibn Abbas, when you see it burst open with fresh blood and fresh blood flows from it,

fresh blood — then know that Abu Abdullah has been killed in it and buried.' Ibn Abbas said: By Allah, I used to guard it more carefully than I guarded some of what Allah the Almighty and Majestic had made obligatory upon me, and I never loosened it from the edge of my sleeve. One night while I was sleeping in the house, I suddenly woke up to find it flowing with fresh blood — and my sleeve had filled with fresh blood. I sat up, weeping, and said: 'By Allah, al-Husayn has been killed.' By Allah, Ali never lied to me in any narration he told me, nor did he ever inform me of anything that would come about without it being exactly as he said — for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) used to inform him of matters that he would not inform anyone else of. So I was seized with terror and rushed out, and that was near the dawn.

key_terms.أَرْضُ كَرْبٍ وَبَلَاءٍ: Land of tribulation and affliction – the epithet given to Karbala in prophetic tradition
key_terms.الْفَرْخُ: The chick/youngling – a term of deep endearment used by Imam Ali and Prophet Isa for Imam Husayn
key_terms.بَعْرُ الظِّبَاءِ: Gazelle manure – the miraculous sign given by Imam Ali that would turn to blood upon Husayn's martyrdom
key_terms.عَاشُورَاء: Ashura – the tenth day of Muharram, the day of Imam Husayn's martyrdom at Karbala
key_terms.نَيْنَوَى: Naynawa – the ancient name of the land where Karbala is located, on the western bank of the Euphrates

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about Karbala when he passed through Naynawa during the march to Siffin?
ai.summary: This extraordinary narration recounts Ibn Abbas's account of accompanying Imam Ali (AS) during the march to Siffin. At the banks of the Euphrates near Naynawa (later Karbala), Imam Ali wept bitterly and shared a vision foreseeing the martyrdom of Imam Husayn (AS). He identified the sacred land, recounted that Prophet Isa (AS) had also wept there and prophesied Husayn's martyrdom, and gave Ibn Abbas a miraculous sign: gazelle manure that would turn to blood upon Husayn's death. Years later, Ibn Abbas witnessed this sign as it came to pass on the day of Ashura.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Sinani (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Yahya b. Zakariyya al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Bakr b. `Abdullah b. Habib narrated to us. He said: Tamim b. Bahlul narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. `Asim narrated to us from al-Husayn b. `Abd al-Rahman from Mujahid from Ibn `Abbas. He said:

I was with Amir al-Mu’minin (as) when he went out to Siffin. When he disembarked in Naynawa, on the coast of the Euphrates, he called out at the top of his lungs: O Ibn `Abbas! Do you recognize this spot? So, I said to him: I do not recognize it, Amir al-Mu’minin. So, `Ali (as) said: Were you to recognize it as I recognize it, you would not be able to cross it without weeping as I weep. He said: Then, he wept for a long time, until his beard was soaked, and the tears dripped onto his chest. We wept with him; while he was saying: Oh, oh! What do I have to do with the Family of Abi Sufyan? What do I have to do with the Family of Harb? The Party of Satan, the Friends of Disbelief! Be patient, O Aba `Abdillah, for they have treated your father similar to how they treat you. Then, he called for water, and he made ablution for prayer. He prayed for as long as Allah willed for him to pray. Then, he repeated his previous words; till he became sleepy at the end of his hour of praying and words.

Then, he regained focus and said: O Ibn `Abbas! So, I said: I am here. So, he said: Shall I not tell you about what I saw in my dream when I laid down? So, I said: Your eyes slept, but you saw goodness, Amir al-Mu’minin. He said: [In my dream,] it was as though I saw men descend from heaven with white flags. Their swords were unsheathed, and they were shining brightly. They created a perimeter around this land. Then, I saw as though these palm trees were striking the ground with their branches, striking with vain blood. It was as though I saw al-Husayn – my son, my youngling, my blood, my mind – was drowning in it, seeking help but not finding help. It was as though the shining men that had descended from heaven were calling to him and saying: “Patience, Family of Muhammad, for you are killed by the hands of the evilest of mankind. This is Paradise, Aba `Abdillah, and it longs for you.” Then, they consoled me, saying: “O Aba’l Hasan! Be glad, for Allah will bring joy to your eye through him on the Day of Resurrection – the Day that the people will be stood before the Lord of the Worlds.”

Then, I regained focus to this. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the Truthful and Trusted Abu’l Qasim (s) told me that I would see this when I would go out to [fight] the betraying people (ahl al-baghi). This is a land of calamity and affliction (karb wa bala’), where al-Husayn and seventeen men from my descendants and the descendants of Fatima will be buried. It is known in the heavens. The land of calamity and affliction is mentioned just as the land of the Two Sanctuaries and the land of Bayt al-Maqdis is mentioned. Then, he said: O Ibn `Abbas! Look for the manure of gazelles for me, for by Allah, I have not lied, nor have I been lied to. It is yellow, and its colour is like saffron. Ibn `Abbas said: So, I looked for it, and I found it gathered. So, I called for him: O Amir al-Mu’minin! I have found what you have described to me. So, `Ali (as) said: Allah and His

The Messenger have spoken the truth. Then, he (as) stood and ran toward it. He picked it up and smelled it. He said: This is precisely it. Do you know, Ibn `Abbas, what this manure is? This is what `Isa b. Maryam (as) smelled. He passed by it with his apostles, and he saw a gazelle here
weeping. So, `Isa (as) sat down, and the apostles sat down with him. He wept, and the apostles
wept too, not knowing why he sat down and why he was weeping. So, they said: “O Spirit of
Allah and His Word! What makes you weep?” He said: “Do you know what land this is?” They said: “No.” He said: “This is the land in which the son of the Messenger, Ahmad, and the son of the Free, the Pure, the Maiden, the one in the likeness of my mother, will be killed and will die in. The clay [here] is sweeter than musk, because it is the clay of the martyred son – such is the clay of the prophets and the children of the prophets. This gazelle speaks to me, and it says that it grazes this land longing for the soil of the blessed son. It believes that it is safe in this land.” Then, he picked up some of the manure with his hand and smelled it. He said: “This manure of the gazelle is fragrant because of the grass of this place.

O Allah! Preserve it so that his father may also smell it, so that it may be a source of consolation and relief for him.” He said: So, it remained for the people until this day, and it has been yellowed due to its lengthy time. This is a land of calamity and affliction. Then, he said at the top of his lungs: O Lord of `Isa b. Maryam! Do not bless his murderers, nor those who help them in it, nor those who desert him. Then, he wept for a long time, and we wept with him, until he fainted onto his face for a long time. Then, he awoke, took the manure, and wrapped it in his cloak. He commanded me to do the same. Then, he said: O Ibn `Abbas! If you see it bursting with congealed blood and dripping in blood,

then know that Aba `Abdillah has been killed here and buried. Ibn `Abbas said: By Allah, I preserved it better than some of the things that Allah obligated over me. I did not move it from the edge of my sleeve. One day, I was sleeping in the house, when I found it dripping congealed blood. My sleeve was filled with congealed blood, so I sat weeping, and I said: By Allah, al-Husayn has been killed. By Allah, `Ali has never lied to me in what he has said to me. He has never informed me of a thing except that it was as he said, because the Messenger of Allah (s) would inform him of things that he would not inform others. So, I panicked, and I left, and that was at Fajr. By Allah, I saw that Medina was filled with fog that could not be seen through. Then, the Sun rose, and I saw that it was as though it was eclipsed. I saw that it was as though the walls of Medina were covered in congealed blood. So, I sat weeping, and I said: By Allah, al-Husayn has been killed. I heard a voice from the direction of the house, and it was saying:
Be patient, O Family of the Messenger,
The feeble son has been killed,
The Trustworthy Spirit has descended,
With weeping and wailing.
Then, it wept at the top of its lungs, and I wept. That hour became resolute with me – it was the month of Muharram, the day of `Ashura’, and ten days had passed from it. I found that he was killed on the same day that we had been informed of. So, I told this hadith to those who were with him, and they said: By Allah, we heard the same thing that you heard while we were in battle. We did not know who [said it], so we believed that it was al-Khidr (as).
